title: Hearing Louis Armstrong and Joe Oliver in Chicago
summary: He recalls Chicago while living with his uncle, Armstrong at the Royal Garden, and Lil Hardin.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well anyway, who did you hear in Chicago when you were out there? Did you hear any music? Yeah.

I used to be out there, 28 in the league, out there, and Louis and them would be out there. Louis was living on, he was playing at the, you see, when Louis come up there, they sent for Lee Collins. You know they sent for René. And René didn't want to go, and Louis went. He was playing at the Royal Garden with Joe Oliver. You understand? You went there? No, I was a little bit too young. You understand what I mean? Well I was in Chicago when they come up there, you see. And I was living on East 36th Street with my uncle, you know what I'm saying? And that's the time I was going to, Al C. Boyd, well he was a cellar player, he used to be up in the old university where I attended school. You understand what I mean?
You were taking music lessons while you were out there too?

No, I didn't know how to play nothing. But I used to hear all the music singing all around Lake Michigan out there, you know, around the swimming hole and things. I'd go down to Grand Park down in Chicago and different things like that.

Well, 30th way from State, well there was nothing at 33rd, 33rd in Indiana, that's where Grand Terrace was, you understand what I mean. Oral Hines was, or when he'd come up, I mean in these late years, well I mean I was down there then when Oral Hines was.
But around 35th and State were you around that area?

I used to go around there and slip in the pool room and shoot proof or something like that, you understand what I mean? But you couldn't get in there? No, no, there wasn't no music around there. You see, it was 30, 40th and Cottage Grove, that's where Joe Oliver was playing. And Miss Lil was playing piano with Joe Oliver and Louis got in the band and she was a graduate of Wilberforce and she got in with Louis and taught Louis how to read, you know, how to read music and things like that. And after Louis started reading music then he started recording for Decca and different things like that, you know, Decca, record recording.
